description: Bus-type annotation classes (PNR_BUS_CLASSES=1): signalling speed and impedance-control requirements per bus type, each value cited. pnr.si.bus_classes derives numeric routing limits from a class plus the board stackup (pnr.si.physics); explicit @pnr-pair annotation values always override derived ones. Times are ps, impedances ohm, lengths mm. A value that the cited document does not specify is null with a note; nothing is invented to fill it.

stub_k.basis: owner decision 2026-09-29: an intermediate-terminal stub (e.g. an ESD branch) must satisfy stub_delay <= k * t_rise_min with k = 0.1, the via barrel included, measured to the pad centre; overridable per class or per annotation ("stub_k")

uncoupled_k.basis: derived rule (not a spec limit): a continuous uncoupled run is treated like a stub-sized discontinuity, uncoupled_delay <= k * t_rise_min with the same k as stubs; overridable per class or per annotation ("uncoupled_k")

fields.kind: differential | single-ended (a @pnr-pair binds differential classes only)
fields.params: optional {name: {default, note}}: numeric class parameters; an annotation overrides them with "params": {...}; used by "expr" fields
fields.signalling: data_rate_bps, t_rise_min_ps, t_rise_max_ps (10-90 %), optional unit_interval_ps: each {value | null, expr?, cite, quote?, note?}
fields.impedance: {required, differential_ohm, tolerance_pct | tolerance_ohm, single_ended_ohm?, common_mode_ohm?, note, cite}; null targets when the document sets none
fields.skew: {max_ps | null, applies_to, cite}: intra-pair skew as time
fields.length: optional total length {max_mm | max_delay_ps: {value | null, expr?, cite}, applies_to}; report-only in v1 (the router checks no total length)
fields.stub_k, uncoupled_k: optional per-class overrides of the library defaults (stub rule stub_delay <= stub_k * t_rise_min; uncoupled rule uncoupled_delay <= uncoupled_k * t_rise_min)

cite.quote: The rise and fall times must be between 4 ns and 20 ns and matched to within +/-10% to minimize RFI emissions and signal skew.

With t_rise >= 4 ns board traces are electrically short, so the target is recommended, not required.
